context:
You asked (13:36 CDT): add real tests to the test files the mutation report called silent, or retire them. A session checked.

What it found: all six files run in every CI build and pass, and a planted failure in each turns the build red, so none is silent in the sense of not running. "Silent" came from the mutation report: it breaks a file's code on purpose and counts which test files notice. These six noticed nothing, because they test other things (how a hook is wired, a platform exit, a wrapper's shape), not the files the report scored them against. Other test files already cover those files fully. It found six files, not the seven you said; none turned up as a seventh.

The pick below is the orchestrator's, taken because it changes no code and you can undo it; it stands unless you change it.

options.gain: Nothing is deleted or duplicated; the real checks stay as they are.
options.how:
No test changes. The six "silent test" notes in the debt list are closed as wrongly attributed, with the reason written down.
Before: six notes say these tests are silent. After: they are closed, and the report's pairing of tests to files is noted as the cause.
options.label: Close the six notes as a mistake in the report
options.lose: If you wanted every one of these files to also test the scored file's logic, that does not happen.

options.gain: Every scored file is tested from more places.
options.how:
Each of the six gets new tests that break when the other file's code breaks.
Before: they pin wiring and shapes only. After: they also pin that logic.
options.label: Add tests of the scored files' logic into these six
options.lose: It repeats tests that other files already have, which makes more to keep up for no new coverage.

options.how:
Remove them from the repo and CI.
Before: they pin hook wiring, a platform exit and wrapper shapes. After: nothing pins those.
options.label: Delete the six files
options.lose: Those behaviours would lose their only tests, for no gain.

title: The six "silent" test files: they are fine, so close the notes about them?
why: They run, they pass and they fail when broken; the report paired them with the wrong files, and the right test files already cover those.
